--- title: "QML - Week 5" subtitle: "Intro to statistical modelling" author: "Stefano Coretta" format: revealjs bibliography: references.bib --- ## Statistical modelling ::: {.cell} ::: ![](/img/data-model.png){fig-align="center"} ## Gaussian models $$y \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)$$ ::: {.cell layout-ncol="2"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-05_files/figure-revealjs/gauss-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-05_files/figure-revealjs/gauss-2.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Simulate Gaussian data ::: {style="text-align: center;"} `rnorm(n, mean, sd)` ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} - `n`: number of obs to generate - `mean`: mean of the Gaussian distribution - `sd`: SD of the Gaussian distribution ::: . . . ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(812) f0 <- rnorm(200, 125, 25) |> round() f0[1:10] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 79 146 111 114 112 147 167 98 143 102 ``` ::: ::: ## f0 density ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-05_files/figure-revealjs/f0-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Simulation vs estimation

::::::: columns :::: column ::: {style="text-align: center;"} **SIMULATION** ::: ![](../img/flaticon/simulation.png){fig-align="center" height="100px"} You have $\mu, \sigma$ and you generate $y$. :::: :::: {.column .fragment} ::: {style="text-align: center;"} **ESTIMATION** ::: ![](../img/flaticon/earth.png){fig-align="center" height="100px"} You have $y$ and you estimate $\mu$ and $\sigma$. :::: ::::::: ::: aside [Simulation icons created by Flat Icons - Flaticon. World icons created by Freepik - Flaticon]{style="font-size: 8px;"} ::: ::: notes When you simulate data, you know the population mean and SD. In research, you don't. You just have observations. Statistical modelling allows you to estimate the mean and SD of the population from the sample. This is statistical inference. **Bayesian Gaussian models** do exactly that: estimate mean and SD. ::: ## Gaussian model of f0 $$\begin{align} f0 & \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)\\ \mu & = ...\\ \sigma & = ... \end{align}$$ ## Gaussian model of f0 $$\begin{align} f0 & \sim Gaussian(\mu, \sigma)\\ \mu & = P_\mu\\ \sigma & = P_\sigma \end{align}$$ ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} $P$ is a generic **posterior probability distribution**. ::: ## Gaussian model of f0: brms ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} f0_tib <- tibble(f0 = f0) library(brms) f0_bm <- brm( f0 ~ 1, family = gaussian, data = f0_tib, file = "cache/f0_bm" ) ``` ::: ## Gaussian model of height: posteriors ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-05_files/figure-revealjs/f0-bm-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## Posterior summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} posterior_summary(f0_bm, probs = c(0.1, 0.9))[1:2,] |> round() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Est.Error Q10 Q90 b_Intercept 126 2 124 129 sigma 27 1 25 28 ``` ::: ::: ## Sample size and uncertainty

![](../img/flaticon/up-and-down.png){fig-align="center" height="100px"} ::: ::: {.column width="33%"} ![](../img/flaticon/question-2.png){fig-align="center" height="200px"} ::: :::::: ::::: columns ::: {.column style="text-align: center;"} the lower the sample size ::: ::: {.column style="text-align: center;"} the higher the uncertainty ::: ::::: ::: aside [Marble icons created by Freepik - Flaticon. Up and down icons created by Freepik - Flaticon]{style="font-size: 8px;"} ::: ## A bit harder: N = 5 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(4256) f0_tib <- tibble(f0 = sample(f0, 5)) f0_bm_small <- brm( f0 ~ 1, family = gaussian, data = f0_tib, file = "cache/f0_bm_small" ) ``` ::: ## A bit harder: N = 5 ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](week-05_files/figure-revealjs/f0-bm-small-plot-1.png){fig-align='center' width=672} ::: ::: ## A bit harder: N = 5 ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} posterior_summary(f0_bm_small, probs = c(0.1, 0.9))[1:2,] |> round() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Est.Error Q10 Q90 b_Intercept 122 7 114 130 sigma 22 7 15 31 ``` ::: ::: ## Statistical modelling ![](/img/data-model.png){fig-align="center"}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
